standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-regular sheaf of ideals is locally generated by a quasi-regular sequence, and then its conormal sheaf is free over the quotient with rank the length of that sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the reference sequence and shows that the number of given elements equals its length.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex of a sequence changes by an invertible change of basis without changing its homology, cited from the more-algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers H1-regularity and Koszul-regularity from the reference sequence to the given one.

standard_prerequisites.name: Invertibility of a matrix over a local ring is detected modulo the maximal ideal, so a matrix invertible at a point is invertible on a neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 4747-4752 and again at 4759-4762
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the change of basis be inverted after shrinking, and gives that the given elements form a basis of the conormal sheaf locally.

core_obligations: Set up the comparison with a reference sequence: pass to an open neighbourhood on which the ideal is generated by a quasi-regular sequence, note that the conormal sheaf is then free of rank equal to the length of that sequence, so the number of given elements equals that length, shrink so that the given elements are sections, and write them as combinations of the reference sequence with a matrix of sections (proof lines 4736-4746).

Invert the matrix: by hypothesis the matrix reduces to an invertible matrix modulo the maximal ideal at the point, hence the matrix is invertible on a smaller neighbourhood, so the given elements form a basis of the conormal sheaf there, which is exactly the assertion that they form a quasi-regular sequence generating the ideal (proof lines 4747-4752).

Handle the two stronger regularity notions: since their hypotheses imply quasi-regularity, the same shrinking and change of basis apply with a reference sequence that is H1-regular, respectively Koszul-regular, and because the Koszul complex on the given sequence is isomorphic to that on the reference sequence, the corresponding regularity carries over (proof lines 4754-4767).
proof_roadmap: Compare the given elements with a local quasi-regular generator and invert the change-of-basis matrix on a neighbourhood (proof lines 4736-4752).
Reuse that shrinking for the stronger notions, where the isomorphism of Koszul complexes transfers H1-regularity and Koszul-regularity (proof lines 4754-4767).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a sheaf of ideals on a locally ringed space which is quasi-regular, H1-regular or Koszul-regular, any elements of the stalk at a point lifting a basis of the conormal space extend, after shrinking, to a sequence of the corresponding type generating the ideal (statement lines 4716-4734). The counted proof is short but complete: it compares the given elements with a local generator, uses that quasi-regularity makes the conormal sheaf free of the right rank so that the two families have the same length, inverts the change-of-basis matrix on a neighbourhood because it is invertible modulo the maximal ideal at the point, and then transfers the stronger regularity notions through the isomorphism of Koszul complexes induced by that invertible matrix (proof lines 4736-4767). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard facts about regular sequences and their Koszul complexes.
